extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel, patent practitioners, applicants, and stakeholders in AI and intellectual property
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating subject matter eligibility (35 U.S.C. 101) of inventions involving artificial intelligence, including how to analyze claims for abstract ideas and whether claims integrate such ideas into practical applications. Meant to assist examiners, applicants, and other stakeholders during examination, appeal, and post‑grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine subject matter eligibility under patent law (35 U.S.C. 101) of AI inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance update builds on previous guidance to provide further clarity and consistency to how the USPTO and applicants should evaluate subject matter eligibility of claims in patent applications and patents involving inventions related to AI technology. It is intended to assist USPTO personnel and stakeholders in determining subject matter eligibility during patent examination, appeal, and post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether a claim recites an abstract idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze whether a claimed invention 'recites an abstract idea' as part of the subject matter eligibility inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance includes discussion and examples addressing particular inquiries such as whether a claim recites an abstract idea. The new examples provide additional analyses under 35 U.S.C. 101 of hypothetical claims to help determine whether a claim is properly characterized as an abstract idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether a claim integrates an abstract idea into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether, even if a claim involves an abstract idea, the claim integrates that idea into a practical application such that it is eligible subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One focus of the examples and guidance is whether a claim 'integrates the abstract idea into a practical application.' The examples illustrate how to apply this consideration across a wide range of technologies to inform examination, appeals, and post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative examples across technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete hypothetical examples to demonstrate application of subject matter eligibility analysis across a wide range of technologies, including AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance update announces three new examples that provide additional analyses under 35 U.S.C. 101 of hypothetical claims. They are intended to assist USPTO personnel in applying the USPTO’s subject matter eligibility guidance to AI inventions during patent examination, appeal, and post-grant proceedings. The examples are available on the USPTO AI-related resources webpage and patent eligibility page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Federal Circuit precedent in eligibility analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate and discuss Federal Circuit decisions relevant to subject matter eligibility in the context of AI inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance update provides additional discussion on certain areas of the guidance that are particularly relevant to AI inventions, including discussions of Federal Circuit decisions on subject matter eligibility, to provide clarity and consistency for examiners and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship guidance for AI-assisted inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance addressing inventorship questions arising from AI-assisted inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release references prior USPTO 'Inventorship guidance for AI-assisted inventions' as part of the broader set of AI-related IP guidance. This guidance informs how inventorship is assessed when AI has played a role in the invention process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of prior art and level of ordinary skill in the art (request for comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit input on what qualifies as prior art and how to assess the level of ordinary skill in the art as they relate to AI and patentability considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO issued a request for comments on the impact of AI on certain patentability considerations, including what qualifies as prior art and the assessment of the level of ordinary skill in the art (comments accepted through the stated deadline). This indicates these factors are relevant to how the USPTO will consider AI-related patentability questions alongside subject matter eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment process for guidance updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for public feedback on the guidance update and examples, with specified deadlines and Federal Register instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will accept public comments on the guidance update and the examples (initially through September 16, 2024; updated to October 16, 2024). The press release directs stakeholders to the Federal Register Notice for instructions on submitting comments, indicating an expectation of stakeholder engagement in refining application of the guidance.
